A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tectonism is an important factor controlling the evolution of intramontane sedimentary systems.
in tectonically and climatically active settings, the processes that govern the evolution of fluvial systems are not limited to the local basin.
the Quebrada del Torobasin is currently in an aggradation stage due to the steepening of the fluvio-deltaic system that connects the basin to the foredeep.
The main takeaway from our work is that

intramontane sedimentary basins can be used as natural laboratories to test models of fluvial sediment transport and to assess the relative roles of climate, tectonic uplift, and lithologic resistance to incision in controlling the geomorphology and sedimentology of these basins.

the geomorphic and stratigraphic evolution of the Toro basin is largely driven by the tectonic uplift of a bedrock zone upstream of the basin and the resulting downstream channel steepening and aggradation.

the geomorphic history of intramontane systems is not simply a reflection of tectonics and climate but also depends on the interplay of the three factors that drive aggradation, denudation, and incision.
